differences.title: 1. DATA STORAGE
differences.leftDesc: Stores data in compressed columnar files, optimized for analytical queries by reading only necessary columns. Highly efficient for aggregations.
differences.rightDesc: Utilizes a hybrid columnar format that also compresses data, but with additional optimizations for both analytical and transactional workloads.

differences.title: 2. ARCHITECTURE
differences.leftDesc: Distributed, shared-nothing architecture where each node has its own CPU, memory, and disk. Scales horizontally by adding more nodes.
differences.rightDesc: Separates storage and compute. Data stored centrally, with independent compute clusters that can access and process the data concurrently.

differences.title: 3. QUERY EXECUTION
differences.leftDesc: Processes data in batches (vectors) rather than row by row. Significantly speeds up analytical operations and reduces CPU overhead.
differences.rightDesc: Massively Parallel Processing (MPP) execution plan distributes query tasks across multiple nodes and cores for parallel processing.

differences.title: 4. SCALABILITY
differences.leftDesc: Scales by adding more servers to the cluster. Compute and storage scale together, requiring careful capacity planning.
differences.rightDesc: Allows independent scaling of compute clusters and storage. Provides flexibility to adjust resources based on specific workload demands.

differences.title: 5. DEPLOYMENT
differences.leftDesc: Can be deployed on-premises or on various cloud providers. Offers greater control over the infrastructure and data.
differences.rightDesc: Fully managed Software-as-a-Service. No infrastructure management required, abstracts away complexities for users.

differences.title: 6. DATA INGESTION
differences.leftDesc: Supports both batch loading and real-time streaming ingestion for near-real-time analytics. Efficiently handles continuous data flows.
differences.rightDesc: Primarily optimized for batch loading. While it supports micro-batching, it's less focused on true real-time streaming ingestion.

differences.title: 7. COST MODEL
differences.leftDesc: Costs are typically based on the hardware resources (CPU, RAM, Disk) you provision for your cluster. Predictable operational costs.
differences.rightDesc: Costs primarily driven by compute credits consumed by queries and data processing. Pay for what you use, can fluctuate.
